content: 1. Diltiazem: Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring and caution are advised when co-administering these agents. 2. Doxycycline: Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora, which is critical for the enterohepatic recirculation of estrogens. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Dronedarone: Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary during co-administration. 4. Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients for potential reduced efficacy of estrogens. 5. Eluxadoline: Eluxadoline increases the systemic levels of conjugated estrogens by reducing their metabolism. Additionally, eluxadoline may increase the systemic exposure of co-administered OATP1B1 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Encorafenib: Encorafenib affects the metabolism of conjugated estrogens by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may lead to increased toxicity or reduced efficacy of these agents. Caution and monitoring are required. 7. Ertapenem: Ertapenem decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora, which impacts the enterohepatic recirculation of estrogens. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Erythromycin Base: Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, erythromycin base can also increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate: Similar to erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It can also increase estrogen levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Erythromycin Lactobionate: Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases estrogen levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Erythromycin Stearate: Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases estrogen levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Eslcarbazepine Acetate: Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 13. Etravirine: Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy of estrogens. 14. Exenatide Injectable Solution: Conjugated estrogens decrease the hypoglycemic effects of exenatide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, necessitating monitoring of glycemic control in diabetic patients. 15. Exenatide Injectable Suspension: Similar to the solution form, conjugated estrogens reduce the hypoglycemic effects of exenatide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 16. Fedratinib: Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Felodipine: Felodipine increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Fleroxacin: Fleroxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Fluconazole: Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Fludrocortisone: Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy of estrogens.
